concepts.gloss_en: The act of seeking/asking 'where is the place of His glory' — the person's searching that revitalizes him, not the phrase itself

The liturgical question 'where is the place of His glory' (from the Kedushah) itself — identified (bechina) with the supernal glory of the sealed utterance, the object rather than the act of seeking it

reason_for_human: Two occurrences are verbal clauses describing the act of seeking ('when he begins to seek' / 'when he seeks and searches'); they differ only by verb choice and are the same concept. The third is the bare liturgical phrase used as a bechina equated with the supernal glory — the object, not the act. Round-1 split holds; under-merge is correct here.
